doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Learning business by mistakes and losing creative time
summary: She took one business course but learned through mistakes, and hopes a manager gives back the creative time she had in school.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did you get any Business of Music courses along the way?

I did one course at Eastman. And it was good. But you don’t really learn anything until you make mistakes, and I’ve made a few this year. That’s part of the reason I needed a good manager. So now, you know, when you’re first writing music, I mean you dream of having a career and people asking you to do music. But when you’re first writing and you’re in school you have so much time just to be creative. And you don’t realize what a

special thing that is, to have nobody know what you’re doing, and to have nobody care. Because you can just be in your world and really bouncing things off yourself and the people are playing it undistracted. Okay? So all of a sudden people, they like your music and they come to you but that creates a whole ‘nother problem. Suddenly you’re distracted too, with putting gigs together, and you don’t have this time to just allow your music to develop and your ideas to fester or whatever they need to do. So I mean what I’m hoping is that now that they’re handling everything, I’m going to be more like I was when I was in school, and more like I was before I was busy. That I’ll be home just thinking about music again. It’s a blessing, wow.
